Lindblad Expeditions: A Pioneering Legacy

“We have always had a very distinct north star,” says Lindblad Expeditions Founder Sven Lindblad. “If we can provide people with extraordinary experiences in the world’s most charismatic places … they form a connection with the natural world that is truly profound.”

That guiding principle can be traced back to 1966, when Sven’s father, Lars-Eric Lindblad, led the first non-scientific voyage to Antarctica, pioneering expedition travel and charting a new course for modern exploration. Sixty years later, that same spirit endures as a global legacy of discovery—driven by curiosity, guided by purpose and rooted in a deep commitment to the planet.

Home About Lindblad Our Story

Lindblad Expeditions was built on a pioneering tradition of exploration that spans more than six decades—one rooted in a simple belief: that experiencing extraordinary places firsthand can inspire a lifelong commitment to protecting them. Through immersive, expert-led expeditions, we create opportunities for travelers to connect more deeply with the natural world. That philosophy has shaped every chapter of our history—from the pioneering voyages of the 1960s to the collaborations, innovations and experiences that continue to define Lindblad Expeditions today.
The Expeditions That Started It All

In 1966, explorer Lars-Eric Lindblad brought the first tourists to Antarctica on a pioneering journey that laid the groundwork for modern expedition cruising. The following year, he led the first international travelers to the Galápagos Islands—another landmark voyage that helped shape this new era of exploration.

Widely regarded as the father of ecotourism, Lars-Eric saw travel not simply as a way to see the world, but as a way to change how people think about it. By opening these remote regions to thoughtful exploration, he demonstrated that travel could be a powerful force for learning and discovery, bringing people closer to wild places and the stories they hold.

In 1979, Lars-Eric’s son, Sven Lindblad, founded Lindblad Expeditions to carry his father’s pioneering vision forward. He built a fleet designed to explore the world’s remote places, expanding the company’s reach to Baja California, the High Arctic and beyond. Under his leadership, Lindblad Expeditions refined the model Lars-Eric first introduced, pairing expeditions guided by experts with itineraries designed to foster a deeper understanding of the planet.
In this short film, Sven reflects on his father’s groundbreaking journey and the enduring purpose that continues to inspire new generations of explorers.
In Collaboration With National Geographic

By 2004, Lindblad Expeditions had established itself as a leader in expedition travel, known for immersive, expert-led exploration and access to remarkable places. That made the company a natural partner for National Geographic. Together, the two organizations forged a groundbreaking collaboration that combined National Geographic’s expertise in science, education and storytelling with Lindblad Expeditions’ unmatched heritage of expedition cruising . With their relationship recently extended through 2040, travelers can look forward to decades of immersive journeys inspired by discovery.
“National Geographic: They represented the world and all that’s in it, and we were the people who took you there.” — Sven Lindblad
Our ships bear the National Geographic name because they are equipped for exploration, with tools and capabilities that deepen discovery.
Immersive, expert-led exploration brings guests closer to wildlife and wild places, revealing the natural world in unforgettable ways.
Our collaboration with National Geographic has been extended through 2040, opening new possibilities for exploration in the decades ahead.
Our Family of Travel Brands

As Lindblad Expeditions has evolved, we've built a collection of travel companies that bring our same spirit of discovery to remarkable destinations on land. Today, our family of travel brands includes Natural Habitat Adventures, Classic Journeys, DuVine Cycling + Adventure Co., Off the Beaten Path and Thomson Safaris. Whether on foot, by bicycle or on safari, these journeys are united by the same values that have always guided Lindblad Expeditions: expert guidance, authentic connections and a deep respect for the cultures and natural environments that make each destination unique.

Lindblad Expeditions has always been guided by a simple principle: The better people understand the natural world, the more they will feel inspired to protect it. With initiatives like the Lindblad Expeditions–National Geographic Fund and sustainable practices built into operations across the fleet, our expeditions are contributing to the health of the places we explore. From supporting local communities to hosting scientists conducting research at sea, each voyage is part of a broader effort to safeguard the places and traditions that make these destinations extraordinary. Guests return home not only with extraordinary memories, but with a deeper appreciation for the planet.

Lindblad Expeditions acknowledges that it takes more than a single business to change the world. As such, they are proud to nurture meaningful relationships with others who align with their guiding principles . In addition to the strategic relationship with National Geographic Society to further conservation, exploration, and education priorities worldwide, Lindblad Expeditions—with partners and friends—is working to make the world a better place.
Both Lindblad Expeditions and Natural Habitat have built their reputation on creating innovative travel opportunities and a deep commitment to sustainable tourism.
Off the Beaten Path o ffers active small-group and private custom journeys around the world, connecting the heart of the traveler with the soul of the place through localized, authentic experiences.
DuVine Cycling + Adventure Co.

DuVine is an award-winning international luxury cycling and adventure company focused on providing immersive cultural experiences across the globe through thoughtfully designed itineraries led by expert local guides.

Classic Journeys handcrafts cultural walking adventures that empower you to see the world on foot and at eye level. They believe that travel—and in particular connecting with other people and cultures when you travel—fuels your soul in a way that very few things do.

The Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) has the most widely recognized certification standard for sustainable marine fisheries. Lindblad Expeditions was the first U.S. signatory to support the MSC, and they continue to purchase from MSC-certified suppliers whenever possible.

Working in partnership with South Pole , the world’s leading developer of international emission reduction projects, Lindblad Expeditions has a portfolio of six carbon project investments that align with the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals. They also offer the opportunity for guests to offset their air travel by purchasing credits from South Pole.
Lindblad Expeditions is a travel partner of the Jeopardy! Clue Crew , helping the roving correspondents gather clues all around the globe for “America’s Favorite Quiz Show.”

Lindblad Expeditions is proud to announce a new photography partnership with OM System (formerly Olympus). OM will supply cameras and lenses for the OM System Photo Gear Locker aboard select ships, and OM photography ambassadors will join select voyages. Best of all, booked guests will have access to exclusive photo tips and discounts on OM gear.
Association of Arctic Expedition Cruise Operators

Lindblad Expeditions is actively involved in Association of Arctic Expedition Cruise Operators (AECO) , which seeks to lead the expedition ship industry with best management practices in the Arctic. They have helped to create polar operation procedures for vessel personnel and guidelines for visitors to this fragile environment.
International Association of Antarctic Tour Operators

Lindblad Expeditions is actively involved in International Association of Antarctic Tour Operators (IAATO) , which seeks to lead the tourism industry with Best Management Practices in the Antarctic. They have helped to create polar operation procedures for vessel personnel and guidelines for visitors to this fragile place.
